scope: Corollary 3.4 (Local matching of scalar graphs) of the manuscript “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (preprints/Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-full-Hausdorff-dimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 30d0c186aa9c697d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the base dimension, algebraic degrees, real comparison balls with fixed holomorphic margins, and d0 < 1. There is ε∗ > 0 with the following property. Let M, ∆ > 0, and put R = M/∆. For sufficiently large R, two lists of real-on-real algebraic sheets cannot satisfy all of the following, with 0 < ε ≤ ε∗ and d ≤ d0: 1. each list has at most Rd+ε members, and each member is within MRε in norm of one common algebraic reference sheet; 2. a subprobability law on pairs of indices and a common real base point in the comparison domain has total mass at least R−ε, with each index-base marginal bounded by Rεπκ,i dz, where the πκ,i are probability weights, separately in each color; 3. on its events, the two values differ by at most ∆Rε, whereas the norm of their difference on the comparison ball is at least MR−ε. Fixed multiplicative constants may be absorbed by decreasing ε∗ or taking R larger.
